citation.title: Improved profile fitting and quantification of uncertainty in experimental measurements of impurity transport coefficients using Gaussian process regression
citation.authors: M.A. Chilenski, M. Greenwald, Y. Marzouk, N.T. Howard, A.E. White, J.E. Rice, J.R. Walk
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/0029-5515/55/2/023012 (this paper's own DOI, PDF p2 header)

scope_read.pdf_pages: 1-21 (p1 publisher cover; journal page n = PDF page n+1)
scope_read.limitations: Figure values were read visually. The open-source code (ref [34]) was not inspected.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The application is spatial profile fitting, not causal time-series estimation
claim_checks.source_finding: Signals were time-averaged over a 0.4 s steady, sawtooth-averaged period of one C-Mod L-mode discharge. TS and ECE ne and Te were then fit as univariate functions of r/a. The prediction at each radius conditions on all observations, including data on both sides.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p8 Sec.4, Figs.5-6; PDF p5 Eqs.(3)-(5)
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: GPR has been used in tokamak analysis to fit time-averaged radial ne and Te profiles with uncertainty estimates on values and gradients [chilenski2015].
claim_checks.qualification: The authors state that inputs may include time (R, Z, phi, t; PDF p4 Sec.3.1). This is an author claim and was not demonstrated in the paper.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: GPR gives posterior mean and covariance, including gradients, with hyperparameters set by MAP or marginalized by MCMC
claim_checks.source_finding: Gradient uncertainty was substantially larger under MCMC than MAP for Te (median 9.0% vs 1.7%).
claim_checks.locator: PDF p5 Eqs.(4)-(5); PDF p10 Table 5; PDF p17 Eqs.(C.14)-(C.19)
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In that application, treating the GP hyperparameters as uncertain materially widened the gradient uncertainty compared with a point estimate [chilenski2015].
claim_checks.qualification: This was shown for a single discharge. It does not transfer to CES reports or to temporal nowcasting.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The GP fits were propagated to downstream code outputs
claim_checks.source_finding: Sixty-five filtered samples were propagated through STRAHL to obtain D and V. MAP and MCMC sampling gave similar D and V results.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Samples drawn from GP profile fits can be propagated through analysis codes for uncertainty quantification [chilenski2015].
claim_checks.qualification: This was offline Monte Carlo propagation. It is not an estimator benchmark.

input_target_timing.inputs: Time-averaged TS ne and Te, plus ECE Te, versus r/a; artificial constraint points (Table 2, PDF p10)
input_target_timing.outputs: Smoothed profiles, gradients, a/L, and samples; STRAHL-derived D and V
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: not_applicable (no CES, BES or ECEI; fit to the same diagnostic data)
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Fits target measured profiles. Physical truth is known only for synthetic data (PDF p19 App.C.6).

validation.independent_truth: Synthetic cubic-spline truth with RMS error versus number of points, 5 noise realizations (PDF p19 Fig.C4). Experimental data were compared against a prior spline fit only.
validation.unknowns: No held-out discharges; behaviour on other discharges is unknown

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: No timing reported; only MCMC settings (400 walkers, 2000 steps, 1000 burn-in, 800x thinning)
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Wall-clock cost and any real-time suitability

forbidden_inferences: That GPR cannot be used causally or temporally
That this paper benchmarked hold, causal or two-sided GP estimators
That its uncertainty figures apply to CES Ti or to KSTAR
That the 11% Te offset relative to splines (PDF p12) is a general result
Any priority conclusion from this paper
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It is the methodological background for the GP family. Our causalGP baseline is our own temporal construction.
